key: Ye Twain have conquered, ne’er have you been conquered: never hath either of the Twain been vanquished. Ye, Indra-Visnu, when ye fought the battle, produced this infinite with three divisions.
s: Closing a hymn that calls Indra and Visnu to the Soma, the verse turns to their battle; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 6.69.8, takes the “three divisions” as worlds, Vedas and speech, an unmeasured whole the two contended for with the Asuras and strode across.

evidence.gloss: O Visnu, you and Indra, the thing over which you contended with the Asuras, standing threefold as worlds, Vedas and speech, and sahasra, unmeasured: that you strode across (vi airayethām means vyakramethām, you strode across).

reason: day.js and verse.js confirm the key (ok true, ref 6.69.8, at [509,8]); 6.69.8 is the last verse of the Indra-Visnu hymn, so the plain sense is faithful. Sāyaṇa glosses tredhā as lokavedavāgātmanā tridhā sthitam, sahasram as amitam, the object as what the two contended for with the Asuras, and vi airayethām as vyakramethām; "whole" follows the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa he quotes, which names the thousand as these worlds, Vedas and speech. Wilson’s note agrees. His alternative (a thousand cows) is not needed. Evidence is a contiguous span of the packet.
